title: SFER Data
text:
Code
librarian::shelf(
  dplyr,
  glue,
  here,
  tidyr
)


Provider Data Assessment


read in data
## === read data from source files (can take a long time)
#source(here("R/getData.R"))
#df <- getData(params$org_id)

# === read from cached file produced by index.qmd
df_allData <- read.csv(here("data", "exports", "allData.csv")) %>%
  filter(source == params$org_id)
df <- df_allData



df$value <- as.numeric(df$value)
df$datetime <- as.POSIXct(df$datetime, format = "%Y-%m-%d")




Code
# Load ggplot2
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(df, aes(x = analyte, y = value)) +
  geom_violin(width = 1.2, adjust = 10, fill = "skyblue", color = "black") +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, outlier.shape = NA) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Analyte", y = "Log10(Value)", title = "Violin + Boxplot")











Code
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

source(here::here("R/presenceTable.R"))

heat_long <- getPresenceHeatmapTable(df)




Code
plotHeatmap(heat_long)











create map with unique points
# check for missing lat/lon
if (all(is.na(df$latitude)) || all(is.na(df$longitude))) {
  cat("Cannot make map: All rows have missing latitude or longitude.")
} else {
  library(leaflet)
  library(dplyr)

  # 1. Filter out rows & keep only one per unique lat/lon
  df_unique_locs <- df %>%
    filter(!is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude)) %>%
    distinct(latitude, longitude, .keep_all = TRUE)

  # 2. Plot all unique points (no clustering)
  leaflet(df_unique_locs) %>%
    addProviderTiles(providers$OpenStreetMap) %>%
    addCircleMarkers(
      lng         = ~longitude,
      lat         = ~latitude,
      radius      = 4,
      color       = "blue",
      fillOpacity = 0.5,
      popup       = ~paste0(
        "Monitoring Location: ", site
      )
      # clusterOptions removed to show every point at all zoom levels
    )
}








visualize distribution of points through time
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)

# Create a dataframe with unique sampling events
sampling_events <- df %>%
  distinct(datetime, site) %>%
  arrange(datetime)




Create time distribution plot
ggplot(sampling_events, aes(x = datetime)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue", color = "white", alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Sampling Events Over Time",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Number of Sampling Events"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )











Code
# Create a heatmap of sampling locations over time
# drop rows with missing dates or IDs
sampling_events <- sampling_events %>%
  filter(!is.na(datetime), !is.na(site))
# if sampling_events is empty, skip this plot
if (nrow(sampling_events) > 0) {
  ggplot(sampling_events, 
          aes(x = datetime, 
              y = site)) +
      geom_point(color = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +
      labs(
        title = "Sampling Locations Over Time",
        x = "Date",
        y = "site"
      ) +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
      )
} else {
  print("No sampling events with valid dates & IDs")
}











Code
date_range <- range(df$`datetime`, na.rm = TRUE)
  cat("Earliest sampling date: ", format(date_range[1], "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "\n")


Earliest sampling date:  2014-12-01 00:00:00 


Code
  cat("Latest   sampling date: ", format(date_range[2], "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "\n")


Latest   sampling date:  2024-11-17 00:00:00

source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # drop any with empty Monitoring.Location.ID
  filter(!is.na(site)) %>%
  # drop any with empty Activity.Start.Date.Time
  filter(!is.na(datetime)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  mutate(datetime = ymd(
          datetime,
          tz = "UTC")) %>%
  distinct()


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(source, site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendallVectorized(
        datetime,
        value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(value),
    min = min(value),
    max = max(value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(value) / mean(value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )

library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}

text:
get data across all programs, filter for analyte
library('here')
library('dplyr')
source(here("R/getAllData.R"))

# read from all source files
# full_df <- getAllData() %>%
#   mutate(
#     source = program,
#     site = Monitoring.Location.ID,
#     datetime = Activity.Start.Date.Time,
#     analyte = DEP.Analyte.Name,
#     value = DEP.Result.Value.Number,
#     units = DEP.Result.Unit,
#     latitude = Org.Decimal.Latitude,
#     longitude = Org.Decimal.Longitude,
#     sample_depth = Activity.Depth,
#     .keep = "none"
# )

# read from cached file produced by index.qmd
full_df <- read.csv(here("data", "exports", "allData.csv"))

df <- filter(full_df, analyte == params$analyte)




create .csv of analyte data
# save df to csv
# reduce to only cols we need & save to csv
df %>%
  write.csv(here("data", "exports", "unified-wq-db-samples", paste0(params$analyte, ".csv")))


Download data for this analyte here

Histogram of value:


display histogram of values
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(df, aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "blue", color = "black") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(title = "Histogram of Values", x = "Value", y = "Log10(Count)")











Reporting Programs:


display reporting programs
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(df, aes(x = source)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(title = "Reporting Programs", x = "Program", y = "Count") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))











Station Statistics:


create station statistics dataframe
source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # drop any with empty Monitoring.Location.ID
  filter(!is.na(site)) %>%
  # drop any with empty Activity.Start.Date.Time
  filter(!is.na(datetime)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  mutate(datetime = ymd(
          datetime,
          tz = "UTC")) %>%
  distinct()


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(source, site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendallVectorized(
        datetime,
        value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(value),
    min = min(value),
    max = max(value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(value) / mean(value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )



# print(head(sample_stats_df))
# # display sample_stats_df with pander
# pander(sample_stats_df)




save stats to csv
sample_stats_df %>%
  write.csv(here(
    "data", "exports", "seasonal-mann-kendall-stats", paste0(params$analyte, ".csv")))


Download data for this analyte’s statistics here


display with gt
library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }

    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}

source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # drop any with empty Monitoring.Location.ID
  filter(!is.na(site)) %>%
  # drop any with empty Activity.Start.Date.Time
  filter(!is.na(datetime)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  mutate(datetime = ymd(
          datetime,
          tz = "UTC")) %>%
  distinct()


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(source, site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendallVectorized(
        datetime,
        value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(value),
    min = min(value),
    max = max(value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(value) / mean(value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )

library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}

title: Phosphorus Report
text:
get data across all programs, filter for analyte
library('here')
library('dplyr')
source(here("R/getAllData.R"))

# read from all source files
# full_df <- getAllData() %>%
#   mutate(
#     source = program,
#     site = Monitoring.Location.ID,
#     datetime = Activity.Start.Date.Time,
#     analyte = DEP.Analyte.Name,
#     value = DEP.Result.Value.Number,
#     units = DEP.Result.Unit,
#     latitude = Org.Decimal.Latitude,
#     longitude = Org.Decimal.Longitude,
#     sample_depth = Activity.Depth,
#     .keep = "none"
# )

# read from cached file produced by index.qmd
full_df <- read.csv(here("data", "exports", "allData.csv"))

df <- filter(full_df, analyte == params$analyte)




create .csv of analyte data
# save df to csv
# reduce to only cols we need & save to csv
df %>%
  write.csv(here("data", "exports", "unified-wq-db-samples", paste0(params$analyte, ".csv")))


Download data for this analyte here

Histogram of value:


display histogram of values
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(df, aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "blue", color = "black") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(title = "Histogram of Values", x = "Value", y = "Log10(Count)")











Reporting Programs:


display reporting programs
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(df, aes(x = source)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(title = "Reporting Programs", x = "Program", y = "Count") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))











Station Statistics:


create station statistics dataframe
source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # drop any with empty Monitoring.Location.ID
  filter(!is.na(site)) %>%
  # drop any with empty Activity.Start.Date.Time
  filter(!is.na(datetime)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  mutate(datetime = ymd(
          datetime,
          tz = "UTC")) %>%
  distinct()


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(source, site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendallVectorized(
        datetime,
        value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(value),
    min = min(value),
    max = max(value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(value) / mean(value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),

  select(
    -z,

library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}

source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # drop any with empty Monitoring.Location.ID
  filter(!is.na(site)) %>%
  # drop any with empty Activity.Start.Date.Time
  filter(!is.na(datetime)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  mutate(datetime = ymd(
          datetime,
          tz = "UTC")) %>%
  distinct()


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(source, site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendallVectorized(
        datetime,
        value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(value),
    min = min(value),
    max = max(value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(value) / mean(value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )

library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}

Station Statistics:


create station statistics dataframe
source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # drop any with empty Monitoring.Location.ID
  filter(!is.na(site)) %>%
  # drop any with empty Activity.Start.Date.Time
  filter(!is.na(datetime)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  mutate(datetime = ymd(
          datetime,
          tz = "UTC")) %>%
  distinct()


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(source, site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendallVectorized(
        datetime,
        value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(value),
    min = min(value),
    max = max(value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(value) / mean(value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )

save stats to csv

library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}
library(dplyr)
library(gt)

# 1) First build your gt table as usual:
gt_tbl <- sample_stats_df %>% 
  gt()

# slope blue (-) to red (+) (0 centered)
tryCatch({
  min_slope <- min(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_slope <- max(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_abs_slope <- max(abs(min_slope), abs(max_slope))
  gt_tbl <- color_column(
    gt_tbl, 
    df     = sample_stats_df, 
    column = "slope",
    palette = rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")),
    domain  = c(-max_abs_slope, max_abs_slope)

}, error = function(e) {

create station statistics dataframe
source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # drop any with empty Monitoring.Location.ID
  filter(!is.na(site)) %>%
  # drop any with empty Activity.Start.Date.Time
  filter(!is.na(datetime)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  mutate(datetime = ymd(
          datetime,
          tz = "UTC")) %>%
  distinct()


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(source, site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendallVectorized(
        datetime,
        value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(value),
    min = min(value),
    max = max(value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(value) / mean(value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )

library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}

Station Statistics:


create station statistics dataframe
source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # drop any with empty Monitoring.Location.ID
  filter(!is.na(site)) %>%
  # drop any with empty Activity.Start.Date.Time
  filter(!is.na(datetime)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  mutate(datetime = ymd(
          datetime,
          tz = "UTC")) %>%
  distinct()


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(source, site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendallVectorized(
        datetime,
        value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(value),
    min = min(value),
    max = max(value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(value) / mean(value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )

library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}
library(dplyr)

  min_slope <- min(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_slope <- max(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_abs_slope <- max(abs(min_slope), abs(max_slope))
  gt_tbl <- color_column(

    df     = sample_stats_df, 
    column = "slope",
    palette = rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")),

create station statistics dataframe
source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # drop any with empty Monitoring.Location.ID
  filter(!is.na(site)) %>%
  # drop any with empty Activity.Start.Date.Time
  filter(!is.na(datetime)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  mutate(datetime = ymd(
          datetime,
          tz = "UTC")) %>%
  distinct()


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(source, site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendallVectorized(
        datetime,
        value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(value),
    min = min(value),
    max = max(value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(value) / mean(value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )

library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}

library(dplyr)
library(reshape2)  # for melt()
library(ggplot2)
library(viridis)
library(RColorBrewer)# for scale_fill_distiller()

# 1. Extract & drop NA
vals_raw <- df$DEP.Result.Value.Number
vals_raw <- vals_raw[!is.na(vals_raw)]

# 2. Log-transform
v1 <- log10(vals_raw + 1)

# 3. Percentile of the log-values
pct1 <- ecdf(v1)(v1)

# 4. Grid dims
N    <- length(pct1)
ncol <- ceiling(sqrt(N))
nrow <- ceiling(N / ncol)

# 5. Pad
pad_len <- (nrow * ncol) - N
p1_pad  <- c(pct1, rep(NA, pad_len))

# 6. Matrix & melt
mat_p1 <- matrix(p1_pad, nrow = nrow, ncol = ncol, byrow = TRUE)
mat_long_p1 <- melt(mat_p1, varnames = c("row","col"), value.name = "pct_log")

# 7. Plot
ggplot(mat_long_p1, aes(x = col, y = row, fill = pct_log)) +
  geom_tile(color = NA) +
  scale_fill_distiller(
    palette   = "Spectral",  # try "RdYlBu", "PuOr", "BrBG", etc.
    direction = 1,           # reverse=FALSE so low values start at red-ish end
    na.value  = "grey90",    # color for the padded NA cells
    guide     = "none"       # hide the legend; remove if you want a colorbar
  ) +
  scale_y_reverse() +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # drop any with empty Monitoring.Location.ID
  filter(!is.na(site)) %>%
  # drop any with empty Activity.Start.Date.Time
  filter(!is.na(datetime)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  mutate(datetime = ymd(
          datetime,
          tz = "UTC")) %>%
  distinct()


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(source, site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendallVectorized(
        datetime,
        value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(value),
    min = min(value),
    max = max(value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(value) / mean(value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )

library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}

  max_slope <- max(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)

    column = "slope",

}, error = function(e) {

title: Chlorophyll_a Report
text:
get data across all programs, filter for analyte
library('here')
library('dplyr')
source(here("R/getAllData.R"))

# read from all source files
# full_df <- getAllData() %>%
#   mutate(
#     source = program,
#     site = Monitoring.Location.ID,
#     datetime = Activity.Start.Date.Time,
#     analyte = DEP.Analyte.Name,
#     value = DEP.Result.Value.Number,
#     units = DEP.Result.Unit,
#     latitude = Org.Decimal.Latitude,
#     longitude = Org.Decimal.Longitude,
#     sample_depth = Activity.Depth,
#     .keep = "none"
# )

# read from cached file produced by index.qmd
full_df <- read.csv(here("data", "exports", "allData.csv"))

df <- filter(full_df, analyte == params$analyte)




create .csv of analyte data
# save df to csv
# reduce to only cols we need & save to csv
df %>%
  write.csv(here("data", "exports", "unified-wq-db-samples", paste0(params$analyte, ".csv")))


Download data for this analyte here

Histogram of value:


display histogram of values
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(df, aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "blue", color = "black") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(title = "Histogram of Values", x = "Value", y = "Log10(Count)")











Reporting Programs:


display reporting programs
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(df, aes(x = source)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(title = "Reporting Programs", x = "Program", y = "Count") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))











Station Statistics:


create station statistics dataframe
source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # drop any with empty Monitoring.Location.ID
  filter(!is.na(site)) %>%
  # drop any with empty Activity.Start.Date.Time
  filter(!is.na(datetime)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  mutate(datetime = ymd(
          datetime,
          tz = "UTC")) %>%
  distinct()


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(source, site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendallVectorized(
        datetime,
        value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(value),
    min = min(value),
    max = max(value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(value) / mean(value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )



# print(head(sample_stats_df))
# # display sample_stats_df with pander
# pander(sample_stats_df)




save stats to csv
sample_stats_df %>%
  write.csv(here(
    "data", "exports", "seasonal-mann-kendall-stats", paste0(params$analyte, ".csv")))

library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}

tryCatch({
  min_slope <- min(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_slope <- max(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_abs_slope <- max(abs(min_slope), abs(max_slope))
  gt_tbl <- color_column(
    gt_tbl, 
    df     = sample_stats_df, 
    column = "slope",
    palette = rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")),
    domain  = c(-max_abs_slope, max_abs_slope)

create station statistics dataframe
source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # drop any with empty Monitoring.Location.ID
  filter(!is.na(site)) %>%
  # drop any with empty Activity.Start.Date.Time
  filter(!is.na(datetime)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  mutate(datetime = ymd(
          datetime,
          tz = "UTC")) %>%
  distinct()


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(source, site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendallVectorized(
        datetime,
        value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(value),
    min = min(value),
    max = max(value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(value) / mean(value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )

library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}

create station statistics dataframe
source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # drop any with empty Monitoring.Location.ID
  filter(!is.na(site)) %>%
  # drop any with empty Activity.Start.Date.Time
  filter(!is.na(datetime)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  mutate(datetime = ymd(
          datetime,
          tz = "UTC")) %>%
  distinct()


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(source, site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendallVectorized(
        datetime,
        value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(value),
    min = min(value),
    max = max(value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(value) / mean(value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )

save stats to csv

  write.csv(here(
    "data", "exports", "seasonal-mann-kendall-stats", paste0(params$analyte, ".csv")))

library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}
library(dplyr)
library(gt)

# 1) First build your gt table as usual:
gt_tbl <- sample_stats_df %>% 
  gt()

# slope blue (-) to red (+) (0 centered)
tryCatch({
  min_slope <- min(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_slope <- max(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_abs_slope <- max(abs(min_slope), abs(max_slope))
  gt_tbl <- color_column(
    gt_tbl, 
    df     = sample_stats_df, 
    column = "slope",
    palette = rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")),
    domain  = c(-max_abs_slope, max_abs_slope)
  )
}, error = function(e) {
  print("Error in slope color column")

create station statistics dataframe
source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # drop any with empty Monitoring.Location.ID
  filter(!is.na(site)) %>%
  # drop any with empty Activity.Start.Date.Time
  filter(!is.na(datetime)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  mutate(datetime = ymd(
          datetime,
          tz = "UTC")) %>%
  distinct()


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(source, site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendallVectorized(
        datetime,
        value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(value),
    min = min(value),
    max = max(value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(value) / mean(value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )

save stats to csv

    "data", "exports", "seasonal-mann-kendall-stats", paste0(params$analyte, ".csv")))

library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}
library(dplyr)
library(gt)

# 1) First build your gt table as usual:
gt_tbl <- sample_stats_df %>% 
  gt()

# slope blue (-) to red (+) (0 centered)
tryCatch({
  min_slope <- min(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_slope <- max(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_abs_slope <- max(abs(min_slope), abs(max_slope))
  gt_tbl <- color_column(
    gt_tbl, 
    df     = sample_stats_df, 
    column = "slope",
    palette = rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")),
    domain  = c(-max_abs_slope, max_abs_slope)
  )
}, error = function(e) {
  print("Error in slope color column")
  print(e)

create station statistics dataframe
source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # drop any with empty Monitoring.Location.ID
  filter(!is.na(site)) %>%
  # drop any with empty Activity.Start.Date.Time
  filter(!is.na(datetime)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  mutate(datetime = ymd(
          datetime,
          tz = "UTC")) %>%
  distinct()


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(source, site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendallVectorized(
        datetime,
        value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(value),
    min = min(value),
    max = max(value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(value) / mean(value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )

library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}
library(dplyr)

  min_slope <- min(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_slope <- max(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_abs_slope <- max(abs(min_slope), abs(max_slope))
  gt_tbl <- color_column(

    column = "slope",
    palette = rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")),

create station statistics dataframe
source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # drop any with empty Monitoring.Location.ID
  filter(!is.na(site)) %>%
  # drop any with empty Activity.Start.Date.Time
  filter(!is.na(datetime)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  mutate(datetime = ymd(
          datetime,
          tz = "UTC")) %>%
  distinct()


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(source, site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendallVectorized(
        datetime,
        value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(value),
    min = min(value),
    max = max(value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(value) / mean(value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )

library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}

Station Statistics:


create station statistics dataframe
source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # drop any with empty Monitoring.Location.ID
  filter(!is.na(site)) %>%
  # drop any with empty Activity.Start.Date.Time
  filter(!is.na(datetime)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  mutate(datetime = ymd(
          datetime,
          tz = "UTC")) %>%
  distinct()


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(source, site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendallVectorized(
        datetime,
        value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(value),
    min = min(value),
    max = max(value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(value) / mean(value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )

save stats to csv

library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}
library(dplyr)
library(gt)

gt_tbl <- sample_stats_df %>% 
  gt()

# slope blue (-) to red (+) (0 centered)
tryCatch({
  min_slope <- min(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_slope <- max(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_abs_slope <- max(abs(min_slope), abs(max_slope))
  gt_tbl <- color_column(
    gt_tbl, 
    df     = sample_stats_df, 
    column = "slope",
    palette = rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")),
    domain  = c(-max_abs_slope, max_abs_slope)
  )
}, error = function(e) {
  print("Error in slope color column")

Station Statistics:


create station statistics dataframe
source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # drop any with empty Monitoring.Location.ID
  filter(!is.na(site)) %>%
  # drop any with empty Activity.Start.Date.Time
  filter(!is.na(datetime)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  mutate(datetime = ymd(
          datetime,
          tz = "UTC")) %>%
  distinct()


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(source, site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendallVectorized(
        datetime,
        value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(value),
    min = min(value),
    max = max(value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(value) / mean(value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )

library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}
library(dplyr)
library(gt)

gt_tbl <- sample_stats_df %>% 
  gt()

tryCatch({
  min_slope <- min(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_slope <- max(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_abs_slope <- max(abs(min_slope), abs(max_slope))
  gt_tbl <- color_column(
    gt_tbl, 
    df     = sample_stats_df, 
    column = "slope",
    palette = rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")),
    domain  = c(-max_abs_slope, max_abs_slope)

title: BBAP Data
text:
Code
librarian::shelf(
  dplyr,
  glue,
  here,
  tidyr
)


Provider Data Assessment


read in data
## === read data from source files (can take a long time)
#source(here("R/getData.R"))
#df <- getData(params$org_id)

# === read from cached file produced by index.qmd
df_allData <- read.csv(here("data", "exports", "allData.csv")) %>%
  filter(source == params$org_id)
df <- df_allData



df$value <- as.numeric(df$value)
df$datetime <- as.POSIXct(df$datetime, format = "%Y-%m-%d")




Code
# Load ggplot2
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(df, aes(x = analyte, y = value)) +
  geom_violin(width = 1.2, adjust = 10, fill = "skyblue", color = "black") +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, outlier.shape = NA) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Analyte", y = "Log10(Value)", title = "Violin + Boxplot")











Code
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

source(here::here("R/presenceTable.R"))

heat_long <- getPresenceHeatmapTable(df)




Code
plotHeatmap(heat_long)











create map with unique points
# check for missing lat/lon
if (all(is.na(df$latitude)) || all(is.na(df$longitude))) {
  cat("Cannot make map: All rows have missing latitude or longitude.")
} else {
  library(leaflet)
  library(dplyr)

  # 1. Filter out rows & keep only one per unique lat/lon
  df_unique_locs <- df %>%
    filter(!is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude)) %>%
    distinct(latitude, longitude, .keep_all = TRUE)

  # 2. Plot all unique points (no clustering)
  leaflet(df_unique_locs) %>%
    addProviderTiles(providers$OpenStreetMap) %>%
    addCircleMarkers(
      lng         = ~longitude,
      lat         = ~latitude,
      radius      = 4,
      color       = "blue",
      fillOpacity = 0.5,
      popup       = ~paste0(
        "Monitoring Location: ", site
      )
      # clusterOptions removed to show every point at all zoom levels
    )
}








visualize distribution of points through time
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)

# Create a dataframe with unique sampling events
sampling_events <- df %>%
  distinct(datetime, site) %>%
  arrange(datetime)




Create time distribution plot
ggplot(sampling_events, aes(x = datetime)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue", color = "white", alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Sampling Events Over Time",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Number of Sampling Events"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )











Code
# Create a heatmap of sampling locations over time
# drop rows with missing dates or IDs
sampling_events <- sampling_events %>%
  filter(!is.na(datetime), !is.na(site))
# if sampling_events is empty, skip this plot
if (nrow(sampling_events) > 0) {
  ggplot(sampling_events, 
          aes(x = datetime, 
              y = site)) +
      geom_point(color = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +
      labs(
        title = "Sampling Locations Over Time",
        x = "Date",
        y = "site"
      ) +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
      )
} else {
  print("No sampling events with valid dates & IDs")
}











Code
date_range <- range(df$`datetime`, na.rm = TRUE)
  cat("Earliest sampling date: ", format(date_range[1], "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "\n")


Earliest sampling date:  2020-01-04 00:00:00 


Code
  cat("Latest   sampling date: ", format(date_range[2], "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "\n")


Latest   sampling date:  2020-12-20 00:00:00

create map with unique points
# check for missing lat/lon
if (all(is.na(df$latitude)) || all(is.na(df$longitude))) {
  cat("Cannot make map: All rows have missing latitude or longitude.")
} else {
  library(leaflet)
  library(dplyr)

  # 1. Filter out rows & keep only one per unique lat/lon
  df_unique_locs <- df %>%
    filter(!is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude)) %>%
    distinct(latitude, longitude, .keep_all = TRUE)

  # 2. Plot all unique points (no clustering)
  leaflet(df_unique_locs) %>%
    addProviderTiles(providers$OpenStreetMap) %>%
    addCircleMarkers(
      lng         = ~longitude,
      lat         = ~latitude,
      radius      = 4,
      color       = "blue",
      fillOpacity = 0.5,
      popup       = ~paste0(
        "Monitoring Location: ", site
      )
      # clusterOptions removed to show every point at all zoom levels
    )
}

visualize distribution of points through time
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)

# Create a dataframe with unique sampling events
sampling_events <- df %>%
  distinct(datetime, site) %>%
  arrange(datetime)




Create time distribution plot
ggplot(sampling_events, aes(x = datetime)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue", color = "white", alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Sampling Events Over Time",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Number of Sampling Events"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )











Code
# Create a heatmap of sampling locations over time
# drop rows with missing dates or IDs
sampling_events <- sampling_events %>%
  filter(!is.na(datetime), !is.na(site))
# if sampling_events is empty, skip this plot
if (nrow(sampling_events) > 0) {
  ggplot(sampling_events, 
          aes(x = datetime, 
              y = site)) +
      geom_point(color = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +
      labs(
        title = "Sampling Locations Over Time",
        x = "Date",
        y = "site"
      ) +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
      )
} else {
  print("No sampling events with valid dates & IDs")
}
